featured_reviews.name: Bhavin Parekh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Shree Vrindavan Restaurant is an excellent vegetarian restaurant recently opened in Mira Road East. Expect a warm, welcoming, and peaceful environment, featuring upscale décor and comfortable seatings for friends and families. Luminious lighting and Melodious music creates a calm and inviting atmosphere, perfect for enjoying a meal. The menu would likely center around traditional vegetarian Indian cuisine, with a special emphasis on dishes that align with the Indian cultural and spiritual values, which is rooted in vegetarianism and purity.
• Starters and Appetizers: Loved its Jamuni paneer tikka which were soft, melt-in-your-mouth texture and Humpty dumpty which was a lovely combination of paneer as well as manchurian. Also loved its special pizza which was crispy, cheesy and awesome in taste.
• Chaat dishes like pani puri, bhel puri, and aloo tikki, offering a burst of flavors with tangy, spicy, and sweet elements.
• Neer Dosa served with sambar, coconut & jagarry and coconut chutney was outstanding.
• Fruit-based desserts like fruit salad with jelly and icecream was superb.
All the delicacies focuses heavily on flavor and the use of fresh, high-quality ingredients. The curries are rich, creamy, and full of authentic Indian spices—using ingredients like cumin, coriander, turmeric, and garam masala. The vegetarian dishes are well-seasoned, offering a balance of spicy, tangy, and savory notes.
Service is friendly, polite and attentive, with knowledgeable staff who can explain the dishes. A visit to a Vrindavan Restaurant is an immersive and delightful experience that transports you to the spiritual world of Vrindavan through food, ambiance, and cultural elements. The dishes are designed to nourish both body and soul, reflecting the essence of Indian vegetarianism—flavorful, wholesome, and steeped in tradition. The combination of great food, warm hospitality, and a peaceful atmosphere makes it an ideal destination for anyone seeking both a satisfying meal and a deeper connection to Indian culture.

featured_reviews.review_text:
This restaurant has become one of those go-to veg restaurants in Mira Road that rarely disappoints. It’s a proper family-friendly place with a wide menu that covers almost everything — South Indian staples, North Indian thalis, Chinese sizzlers, and even snacks for quick bites. You can see why it’s always busy, especially during evenings and weekends.

What stands out most is the consistency in food quality. The paneer dishes are always fresh and soft, with gravies that taste well-balanced rather than overly rich or oily. Their dosas are crisp with good chutneys and sambar, and the pav bhaji is another crowd favorite. flavorful without being too spicy. Portion sizes are generous, so you really feel like you get good value for what you pay.

The service is attentive despite the crowds. Staff are polite, and orders come fairly quickly. The restaurant is also kept clean, which is important when you’re bringing family or kids along.

That said, there are a couple of small areas for improvement. Parking around the area is limited and can be a hassle. On peak days, the wait time for a table can stretch out, which may test your patience a little. Also, while the ambience is clean and functional, it’s not particularly stylish or modern, it’s more about comfort than fine dining.

Overall though, this place hits the right notes with quality veg food, quick service, and affordable pricing. It’s reliable, family-friendly, and definitely one of the better veg dining spots in Mira Road.

Having said that, the preparation was great and is strongly recommended for those who are ok with maida noodles and/or regular rice. I would love to order it again, if they start making in rice noodles.

I recently visited 'Shree Balaji - Pure Veg Restaurant' located just a 5-minute walk from my home on a weekday, with my family. The restaurant had a nice interior and was a great place for family outings. However, our dining experience didn't live up to our expectations.

We ordered a variety of dishes, including Veg Manchow soup, All Toppings Pizza, Chinese Draft Sizzler, Mexican Nachos Cheese Ball, French fries and Italian Paneer Tikka with Curd Dip. Unfortunately, the food didn't impress us.

The All Toppings Pizza was just a name that actually had very few toppings and the biggest disappointment was the Mexican Nachos Cheese Ball. It was raw inside and the nachos weren't fresh. We had to return it. The only enjoyable part of the meal was the 300ml glass bottle ThumsUp i had afterward.

In conclusion, despite the pleasant ambiance, the restaurant fell short in terms of taste and quality. The lackluster flavors, especially with the raw cheese ball and underwhelming pizza, left us dissatisfied. Hopefully, the restaurant will work on improving the quality of their dishes to become a better choice for vegetarian cuisine in the neighborhood.

Overall Ratings:
Food: 3/5
Ambiance: 4/5
Service: 4/5
Quantity: 4/5
Value for Money: 3/5
